title: Implement GraphQL Request Batching Support
description: The SocialPulse Gateway currently processes one GraphQL operation (query or mutation) per HTTP request. To improve client-side performance and reduce network overhead, a new feature is required: GraphQL request batching. This will allow clients to send an array of GraphQL operations in a single HTTP request and receive an array of results in the response. This task is divided into multiple sessions. The first session will focus on the initial data structure and parsing logic. The second session will require the agent to resume the work, understand the partial implementation, and complete the request handling and response aggregation logic.

project_spec.name: SocialPulse Gateway
project_spec.description:
SocialPulse Gateway is a high-performance API gateway written in C that unifies all traffic flowing into a constellation of micro-services powering a next-generation social network. Acting as both a REST and GraphQL façade, it brokers friend-graph interactions, real-time reactions, group collaboration and content discovery while enforcing enterprise-grade security, rate-limiting and versioning.  

Designed with Clean Architecture, SocialPulse Gateway sits at the outermost interface layer, isolating volatile concerns (network, transport, authentication) from the stable domain of social operations (follow/unfollow, timeline aggregation, trending topics). Each use-case is exposed through a Command/Query split so write actions—posting, commenting, reacting—never mingle with read-optimized queries—feed retrieval, search, analytics—guaranteeing clarity, testability and scalability.  

To deliver a truly social-centric experience, the gateway embeds social-aware features such as relationship-based rate limits (closer friends can interact more often), community-scoped version negotiation, and GraphQL federation that understands user privacy scopes. Fine-grained monitoring and structured logging feed a metrics pipeline, enabling community-health dashboards while predictive caching keeps viral content hot at the edge.
dependencies: hiredis (Redis client used for response_caching & rate_limiting buckets)
libpq (PostgreSQL client for configuration & version registry)
clang-format & cpputest (code quality & unit testing suite)
